title: TapeLift - Non-invasive analysis of epidermal methylomes for skin cancer prevention
summary:
We are working on a project to develop a tool that can predict a person’s risk of getting skin cancer. The tool will use different types of information, mainly DNA patterns called methylation profiles, as well as pictures and moisture measurements of the skin.
To do this, we will look at skin samples from about 5,000 healthy people of different ages and genders, because age and sun exposure are important factors for skin cancer.
In our lab at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), we use a painless and non-invasive method to collect tiny amounts of DNA from the very top layer of the skin using sticky strips. We have found that even this small amount of DNA is enough to get the information we need for the project.
The study also includes a short questionnaire to learn about people’s habits and other background information.
We believe that creating this tool, based on a fast, simple, and pain-free sampling method, could help prevent keratinocyte carcinomas, which are the most common type of skin cancer in the world.

interventions.name: Approximately 5000 donors whose ages and genders should be evenly distributed between the following decades of life: 18-29 years, 30-39 years, 40-49 years, 50-59 years, 60-69 years, and finally >70 years.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants must have given their written informed consent, and their ages and genders should be evenly distributed between the following decades of life: 18-29 years, 30-39 years, 40-49 years, 50-59 years, 60-69 years, and finally >70 years. Participants must be able to understand the full nature and purpose of the study, including possible risks and adverse effects.
Exclusion criteria:
Presence of any evident skin disease at the sampling site.
